verdict.reasoning: Patient states: "it's been happening for about, three days now" referring to the diarrhea.

Doctor asks frequency; patient answers "Uh, four to five." Doctor clarifies type as water vs loose; patient replies "It probably depends on the time of day..." and doctor summarizes "Bit of both," indicating watery or loose stools.
Patient describes: "it's pretty standard diarrhoea, where it's was like a little bit of abdominal pain." This supports mild abdominal pain.
Patient clearly states: "I threw up once, yeah."
Doctor asks: "is there any blood or mucus?" Patient responds: "No blood" and then after explanation of mucus: "No."

Regarding fever: Patient says "Uh, maybe a little bit, but... it hasn't been, that in particular hasn't been too worrying." Regarding appetite and fluids: "Appetite loss I guess worse than normal..." and doctor confirms "you're still able to drink quite a bit yeah?" Patient: "Yeah yeah yeah." This supports possible low-grade fever, decreased appetite, and maintained oral intake.
Patient notes: "no travels recently" and in response to question about "anything from outside? Nothing dodgy" says "No, no no no," supporting no recent travel or suspicious food.
Patient states: "Probably I I had asthma... or, or I don't know I guess I still have it."

On inhalers, patient says: "Lexapro." Doctor clarifies and repeats as "Laxepro" and asks about color: "Is it like a blue colour?" Patient replies: "Yellow." Thus transcript documents an inhaler named (as heard) 'Laxepro', yellow.
Doctor asks: "Any allergies?" Patient responds: "No... Nothing, yeah, nothing."

Patient says: "my dad had hypertension... Has hypertension. Had hypertension. Yeah he died of bowel cancer ten years ago." Doctor confirms: "Bowel cancer. Ten years ago. And how old was he when he died?" Patient: "Uh, sixty-two."
Doctor comments: "you’re still drinking plenty and you look like you're not dehydrated which is a good sign," indicating visual impression of no dehydration.

All elements are in transcript: diarrhea ~3 days ("it's been happening for about, three days now"), mild abdominal pain ("a little bit of abdominal pain"), single emesis ("I threw up once"), 4–5 BMs/day ("Uh, four to five"), no blood or mucus ("No blood" and "No" to mucus), tolerating fluids ("you're still able to drink quite a bit" / "Yeah yeah yeah"), and no travel/food exposures ("no travels recently" and "No, no no no" to dodgy food).

Doctor advises: "You still need to drink plenty of water because you're losing a lot of fluids" and later: "you could get something called Dioralyte over the counter. So, it helps to uh, replenish your, the salts that you've been, that's lost through going to the toilet."

Doctor: "things that one would advise is a soft diet. So avoid dairy, fish, meat, eggs, while you're having the diarrhea." Then defines soft diet as "crackers, toast, jam..." and later: "Once you are able to... you can start off with some just boiled vegetables and mash." Also: "although you can't milk is not a good idea, yoghurts are a good idea because they are probiotics, it help to build up the normal... gut bacteria back." Mashed potatoes are a reasonable inference from "mash" in context of vegetables; overall recommendations match.

Doctor instructs: "Once you're OK with that for about forty-eight hours then you can start having meat. So just don't have meat once you feel like you're slightly better..." and reiterates: "Forty-eight hours you're not having any diarrhea, you're fine then you can go and start having meat, egg, fish and all."

Doctor gives safety netting: "if your diarrhoea doesn't go away in a week's time, or if you're passing blood, we need a stool sample" and "If you're again... going about six to eight times a day... you might need to go into hospital at that point in time. If that happens you get in touch with us again." These cover persistence >1 week, blood, increased frequency, and escalation for dehydration risk.

Doctor states: "If that happens you get in touch with us again, all right?" and closes with availability via app, implying contact service if worsening or concerns; this is standard safety-net phrasing present in transcript.
Doctor: "you know you can actually, uh, all this is all recorded in your app. So you can go back. I'll put that all in detail so... you can go back and read, read the notes."
